title: A 3D space combat roguelite with Claude Code and Codex for art & models.
author: Mojo2013
selftext:
Hey all! I'm a solo dev, and Void Squadron is my 3D space combat roguelite, made in Unity.



AI did a lot of the heavy lifting: Started with Cursor earlier this year, then finished with Claude Code and Codex. Codex painted the steam capsules, 2D art and did some of the 3D models. I handled the design, direction and a lot of playtesting. This game was also built on top of a Unity asset pack.



You dogfight pirates & aliens, mine asteroids for upgrades and command a squadron of wingmen through three sectors and three bosses. There's two-player co-op too.  


Happy to answer anything about the workflow. It's nice to find a community that doesn't dismiss months of effort over 'AI Slop'. Thanks for watching!



Steam: [Void Squadron](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5320150/Void_Squadron/)

comments.author: Rcraft
comments.body:
Has anyone bought/played your game yet? How much time did you spend playing or watching people play your game?

I don't see a demo and would imagine that limits a lot of people from trying your game since most AI disclosed games have a poor reputation for being good.

replies.author: Mojo2013
replies.body:
I launched it less than 24 hours ago, so far 7 sales. I am the only play tester. Once I play the game and it feels good to me and I see no more issues, I launch. Then players find bugs and ask for improvements and such.

I've experimented on my other games with demos and free to play, but my most succesful games have just been straight up releases like this.

replies.author: Rcraft
replies.body:
Interesting, thanks for sharing! Good luck, the trailer looks pretty well done and the Steam page seems to hit all of the marks. 

Did you develop games before using AI in the process, too?

replies.author: Mojo2013
replies.body: I made an incremental web game back in 2012 and then finally figured out steam game development in 2022
